exposure: Traumatic experiences (childhood and adulthood physical and sexual abuse)
outcome: Symptom profiles of major depressive disorder
cohort: The study participants were Black and White women who screened positive for postpartum depression and accepted a psychiatric diagnostic interview at an urban maternity hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
finding: Among screen-positive participants, there was no significant difference in the rate of major depressive disorder between Black and White women, but bipolar disorder significantly differed, and symptom profiles for major depressive disorder also differed.
